newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal unit closes debt issue.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal unit closes debt issue.

text.p: Bank of Montreal brokerage unit Nesbitt Burns Inc said on Wednesday that it closed a C$1.35 billion debt issue, the largest ever non-sovereign issuance in Canada.
Nesbitt said it issued two investor certificates through its new special purpose vehicle, Master Credit Card Trust.

The first two certificates in a series were issued today with the following terms: Series 1997-1, having a par value of C$550 million, a coupon of 5.76 percent and an expected maturity date of August 21, 2002; and Series 1997-2, having a par value of C$800 million, a coupon of 6.15 percent and an expected maturity date of December 21, 2004.

Nesbitt said it created Master Credit Card Trust to purchase the consumer credit card receivables of Bank of Montreal and to finance the acquisition through the issuance of credit card-backed investor certificates.

Nesbitt said both series of investor certificates were rated AAA by both Moody's Investors Service Inc and Canadian Bond Rating Service Inc. The investor certificates were sold by way of private placement to Canadian institutional investors.

"This transaction represents the first major non-mortgage related commitment made by a Canadian bank to the domestic securitization market,'' said Ian Bandeen, Nesbitt Burns managing director, securitization and structured finance.
"This is likely just the beginning of a significant wave of securitizations that you should expect to see emanating from other members of the Canadian banking community over the coming months."
